summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and a history of TIPS placement, was admitted for coffee ground emesis and melena, concerning for upper GI bleeding. His symptoms resolved, and recent endoscopic findings suggested portal hypertensive gastropathy and esophagitis as likely sources. He underwent a TIPS revision with balloon dilation, reducing the portosystemic gradient from 20 to 13 mmHg, and sclerotherapy of gastric varices. Two therapeutic paracenteses removed 7L and 4L of fluid, with no evidence of infection. He was managed with octreotide, pantoprazole, and ciprofloxacin prophylaxis. Hyponatremia was monitored and remained stable. His insulin was adjusted, and glipizide was held. Palliative care was consulted per patient request. He improved clinically, with stable vital signs and labs, and was discharged home with follow-up plans, medication adjustments, and recommendations to restart aspirin when bleeding risk decreases.
